name: ModelGain Queue Health for Action Scheduler – Scheduled Actions Monitor
author: ModelGain.com

sections.description:
Action Scheduler runs the background work behind WooCommerce, subscription renewals, emails, webhooks, imports and many other plugins. When the queue stalls, orders and emails are late, and Tools → Scheduled Actions shows thousands of rows without telling you what is actually wrong.

ModelGain Queue Health for Action Scheduler adds one diagnostic screen under Tools → Action Scheduler Health that answers the questions you ask during an incident:

  • Is the backlog abnormal? Pending, Past Due, recent Failed and long-running action counts, plus the age of the oldest overdue action.
  • Is the runner working? Checks WP-Cron, the default Action Scheduler runner hook and the next scheduled queue run.
  • Which hook is the problem? Ranks the hooks with the strongest overdue or failure signal.
  • Which plugin owns it? Maps currently registered callbacks back to a likely plugin, must-use plugin, theme or WordPress core file.
  • What failed? Recent failure evidence, without exposing Action Scheduler arguments.
  • Need help from a developer or host? Copy a privacy-conscious support report.
  • See it in Site Health. A Critical queue shows up in Tools → Site Health next to other site problems.

States are Healthy, Review and Critical. A small transient backlog can be normal, and ownership evidence does not prove that a plugin is the root cause, so the plugin gives conservative guidance instead of alarms.

Safe by design

The plugin is read-only. It does not cancel, delete, rerun, reschedule or edit any action, so it is safe to install on a live store during an incident. It makes no external API calls and does not send telemetry.

It works with any active Action Scheduler runtime, whether it comes from WooCommerce, WooCommerce Subscriptions, a marketing or SEO plugin, or a theme.

Pro add-on: get warned before customers notice

The free plugin is complete for diagnosing the queue and stays free, with no locked features or license prompts. If you want the queue watched for you, the optional Pro add-on adds:

  • Scheduled background checks: hourly, twice a day or daily.
  • One email when the queue becomes Critical (or Review, if you choose), not on every check.
  • A failure-spike email when many actions failed since the previous check, and an optional “healthy again” email.
  • History of the last 48 checks with state, past due, failures, long-running actions, the top hook and its likely owner.
  • CSV export of the history.
  • WP-CLI: wp modelgain-queue-health check --fail-on=critical exits with code 1 when the queue is Critical, for server cron, uptime tools and deploy checks.

Pro is $19.99 per year or $29.99 once for lifetime use, per site, sold through Freemius. Like the free plugin, it never changes scheduled actions.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins → Add New by searching for “ModelGain Queue Health”, or upload the ZIP.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Open Tools → Action Scheduler Health.

If no active plugin or theme has loaded Action Scheduler, the plugin will simply report that no Action Scheduler runtime was detected.
sections.faq:
Why are my WooCommerce scheduled actions past due?

Common causes are WP-Cron not running (low traffic or DISABLE_WP_CRON without a server cron), one plugin’s hook failing or running very long, or a large backlog after an import. This plugin shows which of these signals is present and which hook and plugin are most involved.

Does this plugin delete or repair scheduled actions?

No. The plugin is deliberately read-only. It diagnoses the queue and gives conservative next-step guidance, but it does not mutate scheduled actions.

Is every past-due action a problem?

No. A short-lived backlog can occur during normal queue processing. The health state considers counts, age, recent failures, long-running work, and runner signals together.

How does plugin ownership detection work?

When a callback for a problematic hook is currently registered, the plugin inspects the callback source file and maps it to WordPress core, a plugin, a must-use plugin, or a theme. This is evidence about ownership, not proof that the component caused the failure.

Does the support report include order or customer data?

The report intentionally excludes Action Scheduler arguments. It contains queue counts, runner diagnostics, hook names, and likely owner information.

Does it require WooCommerce?

No. It works with any active Action Scheduler runtime, whether Action Scheduler is provided by WooCommerce or another plugin or theme.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes. The free plugin is complete for diagnosing the queue and will stay free. The separate Pro add-on checks the queue on a schedule, keeps a history of checks, emails you when the queue becomes Critical or failures spike, exports the history as CSV and adds WP-CLI commands for monitoring. The small Pro card on the health screen can be hidden with one click, and the free plugin never asks for a license.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Clearer plugin name, description and FAQ for people troubleshooting past-due WooCommerce scheduled actions.
  • A small, dismissible card on the health screen describes the optional Pro add-on. It is hidden when Pro is active. No feature of the free plugin changed or became limited.
  • Uninstall also removes the per-user “hide Pro card” preference.

1.0.0

  • Added a Site Health test that reports Healthy, Review or Critical queue state (cached for 10 minutes).
  • Added the modelgain_as_queue_health_loaded action so add-ons can reuse the read-only checker.
  • Uninstall removes the Site Health cache.

0.1.1

  • Fixed paths and unique prefixes following WordPress.org review.
  • Renamed plugin to ModelGain Queue Health for Action Scheduler.

0.1.0

  • Initial read-only queue health dashboard.
  • Added overdue, recent-failure, and long-running action diagnostics.
  • Added dominant-hook ranking and callback-based ownership evidence.
  • Added runner diagnostics and a privacy-conscious support report.
